cohort: 2791 children of women participating in the 'Seguimiento Universidad de Navarra' cohort
finding: Children born by cesarean delivery have higher average BMI z-scores and an increased risk of overweight/obesity compared to children born vaginally, even after adjusting for potential confounders and accounting for sibling correlations.
mod_finding: This study compared the risk of overweight/obesity in children born via cesarean delivery versus vaginal delivery.
followup_time: Various age strata, but no specific ages mentioned
